plane-v2.note: rho_floor and rho_floor_tracking follow the re-measured oracle hold (oracle audit: on plane and plane_sine the shipped planner flies the capture of the initial altitude offset and, once the aircraft has settled, a planner over the cascaded PID's airspeed loop with a decaying step holds). They are the NEA reference: no reward reads them, so the environment's behaviour is unchanged. e_floor stays: plane's is the 1 m altimeter resolution, and plane_sine's 1.26 m is within 1.5x of the 1 m resolution that would replace it. The plane MPC does not read rho_floor_tracking (it plans on a fixed objective scale per task), so the holds that set the new values were measured with the oracle the rows were recorded with. The PlaneParams default in plane/env.py moved too, which moves plane_sine's and plane_energy's stamps as well; both override it.

plane_energy-v3.note: v3: e_floor 4.55 -> 1.20 m (oracle audit, 2026-10). 4.55 m was an earlier oracle's hold, taken before its moves toward the next target were separated from its hold; 1.20 m is the current oracle's best per-seed hold, 1.198 m, rounded. failure_cost follows (2 x (12192 / 1.20)^2), and rho_floor = rho_floor_tracking = (1.1773 / 1.20)^2 from the hold re-measured under the new floor. Re-stamped in place when plane's rho_floor moved: the PlaneParams default in plane/env.py changed, and plane_energy overrides it, so its reward and floors are unchanged.
